answer: Each agent must place a refundable stake in a shared registry before its votes count; the registry rate-limits how much influence one stake can buy and slashes it when signed actions prove fraudulent. A raven agent can still join under a fresh name, but multiplying identities no longer multiplies voting power: the attacker must lock more capital for longer, risk losing it, and pay transaction costs. At a harbor, honest agents can challenge suspicious claims with evidence, while an onyx audit log makes the stake and penalties verifiable.
